scope: Read-only complementary source-build UI boundary verification. Real mounted Database DOM events under happy-dom and the real shared authoring controller/compiler/store/history. Not whole UI acceptance, visual approval, browser QA, app build, CSS gate, or remote persistence verification.
outcome: Eight complementary probe cases executed once: five passed and three genuine behavioral failures. Project-keyed proposal authority remains intact, but global object target fields authorize a fresh build in another project with a coincident map ID. Blank seeds silently become zero. Invalid object coordinates are correctly rejected by the compiler, then leave an uncorrectable pending proposal with no mounted clear action.

findings.title: Object target fields cross project identity and authorize a new build in the wrong project
findings.mechanism: buildSeed/buildMapId/rect/entry are module-global mutable fields. Their reset function has no production caller beyond re-export. Shared authoring handles and build disclosure instead reset on spatialProjectKey changes. Selecting a canonical object in the new project makes destReady true from the previous project's fields and creates a fresh correctly-issued preview against the wrong project's coincident map. This is not acceptance of a stale A preview; A's proposal correctly disappeared before B's Build.
findings.reproduction: In project A, select hearth-design, enter seed 19, stamp-target rect 3,3,3,3 and entry 1,1, then Build. Use real store.replaceProject to install independent project B with a distinct project key and a same-ID map named Project B coincident map. Re-render Database and select B's canonical object using mounted card events. Enter no target or seed fields in B. Click mounted Build and Apply.
findings.requiredCorrection: Bind object Build fields to the actual spatial project identity or invalidate the target on project change, so a coincident map ID cannot reuse another project's destination consent.

findings.title: An empty numeric seed is coerced to an explicit zero seed
findings.mechanism: The mounted number field change handler calls Number(seed.value). Clearing the field produces Number('') === 0, which passes the real backend Number.isSafeInteger check. The rerender and proposal then adopt zero although the user provided no number. All three domains share this handler.
findings.reproduction: Select the canonical space, clear spatial-build-seed through its real change event, click Build.
findings.requiredCorrection: Preserve the invalid/empty numeric-input state at the mounted input boundary and reject it instead of manufacturing zero. Explicit numeric zero need not be prohibited.
findings.causalControls: Mounted decimal seed 1.5 and unsafe integer 9007199254740992 were both rejected with no proposal, preview, or live mutation.

findings.title: A rejected object target traps the mounted UI in an immutable pending proposal
findings.mechanism: Build stores buildInput before real compile validation. Entry X=-1 is rejected at compile.target.entry.x, so no preview exists, but the invalid proposal remains pending. Correcting the mounted field changes the input; the existing pending-input guard rejects it with build-proposal-pending. The Stage action inventory exposes no clear/cancel action and no production UI path calls clearAuthoringSession. Removing the immutable pending guard is not the required remedy: valid pending proposals must retain their exact inputs.
findings.reproduction: Enter the valid explicit object target except entry X=-1, click Build and observe the compiler path error. Correct entry X to 1 in the mounted field and click Build again.
findings.requiredCorrection: Provide an explicit reachable clear/cancel-and-retry route, with truthful draft-discard semantics, or avoid pinning a numerically rejected attempt before it can become a valid proposal. Preserve exact valid-pending input retention.
findings.causalControls: The separate real clearAuthoringSession boundary does release the proposal, and a subsequent mounted Build at seed 31 obtains a different fresh root. That API-only clear control is not proof of mounted recovery.

confirmedBoundaries: Canonical source resolution uses canonicalSource plus own library membership, not card label, coincident local ID, or compatibility record identity. All eight producer tests were read; none was rerun here.

An explicitly entered map/rect/entry is allowed to differ from editorState.currentMapId and selection. A mounted causal-control test passes with that mismatch. This is deliberate explicit targeting, not an implicit current-map/start-map/selection fallback defect.

Object numeric entry X=-1 reaches and is rejected by the real compile parser. Source inspection confirms rect x/y >=0, width/height >=1, and entry x/y >=0 are safe integers. The coordinate defect reported here is recovery after rejection, not absent backend numeric checks.

The exact pending source, seed, destination and root survive object/space tab changes and an attempted competing object Build. A newer source width edit remains in the draft; returning to Spaces, rebuilding and applying adopts the exact preview project, retains width 14 and one root, and records one history entry.

freshSpatialId scans all source-library IDs and occurrence IDs in visibleAuthoringProject. Matching pending inputs reuse their allocated root; explicit shared clear followed by a new mounted Build produces a distinct root with no prior output in the new preview.

A real project switch clears the shared proposal and issued-preview view before the next build. The remaining cross-project defect is the lifetime of the newly added field state, not a stale-handle bypass.
